page: The Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is a virtual server instance within the High Performance lineup, driven by an AMD EPYC processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction set extensions including AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory comprises 4.0 GB of RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU thread. Storage is locally attached via a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. The server does not contain dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results reflect the shared-thread configuration and 2.0 GHz clock speed of the underlying AMD EPYC silicon. In stress-ng evaluations, the instance produced a single-core score of 2263.16, placing it in the average tier, while the multi-core result of 4483.12 landed in the lower quartile. Geekbench scores registered 1116.0 for single-core execution and 2013.0 for multi-core workloads, with compiling tests in Clang reaching 2024.0. Memory throughput testing revealed 168.23 GB/s on 16 KB cached reads, dropping to 20.06 GB/s on 256 MB uncached reads and 20.37 GB/s on uncached writes. Database and key-value benchmarks showed 1.85 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside a PassMark database score of 566.4.

With its entry-level shared CPU topology, the vhp-2c-4gb-amd balances modest processing throughput against the inclusion of fast local NVMe storage. Because the two vCPUs share a single physical core, sustained parallel computational loads experience core-sharing overhead. However, the 100 GB NVMe volume delivers fast local input/output relative to the server footprint, making it cost-efficient for lightweight baseline services rather than compute-intensive tasks. This profile makes the instance appropriate for staging environments, lightweight web servers, reverse proxies, dev/test CI/CD workers, and low-traffic utility applications.
description: The Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is an entry-tier virtual server within Vultr's High Performance family, equipped with 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC core running at 2.0 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 4.0 GB of RAM alongside 100 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, without GPU acceleration. CPU benchmark metrics show average single-core capacity with a stress-ng score of 2263.16, while multi-core performance reaches 4483.12, reflecting the shared single-core hyperthreaded design. Uncached memory write throughput achieves 20.37 GB/s, and Redis SET throughput measures 1.85 million operations per second. Because processing relies on shared CPU scheduling, computational efficiency favors bursty or moderately utilized applications over prolonged heavy compute. The vhp-2c-4gb-amd is best suited for lightweight web serving, development and testing environments, staging deployments, and low-traffic internal utility microservices.
